Age fit: Sentences stay short for ages 7 to 11. The task is one tap: turn the square and compare corners.
Whether it teaches the objective: After the tap, a child can point to four corners on the square and none on the circle, and can say a turn did not add sides.
Interaction quality: The turn is the teaching move. The page rotates shape A and, when dimension is 3d, opens a side view of the same shapes.
Mobile feel: The turn control is a full-width button with a tall tap target. The canvas uses the width of a phone.

observationPrompts: How many corners does the square have after the turn?
What does the side view look like?

misconceptions.belief: Turning a shape gives it new sides.
misconceptions.response: A turn moves the shape. The square still has four sides and four corners.
